Input is not trimmed; values must fit in u32.

title: Exercise 03
instruction: Write at least six tests for Counter, using nonnegative maxima: new(3) starts at 0 and is not full; increment raises the value and returns true; reaching max makes is_full true; another increment returns false and leaves the value unchanged; reset returns to 0 and permits incrementing again; new(0) is already full and cannot increment. Include a sequence of calls in at least one test.

title: Exercise 04
instruction: Write at least seven tests: three non-panicking get_element cases (first, last, and a one-element slice), two #[should_panic] cases (empty slice and index equal to length), and two safe_divide cases (10 / 2 → Some(5), division by zero → None). Use expected = "out of bounds" for at least one panic test. Integer division truncates toward zero. Exclude i32::MIN / -1 overflow.

title: Bmi category
instruction: Implement `bmi_category(weight_kg, height_m)`. Calculate `weight_kg / (height_m × height_m)`. Return `"underweight"` below 18.5, `"normal"` from 18.5 to below 25, `"overweight"` from 25 to below 30, and `"obese"` at 30 or above. Assume positive height and weight.

title: Describe temp
instruction: Implement `describe_temp(celsius)`. Return `"freezing"` below 0, `"cold"` from 0 to below 15, `"warm"` from 15 to below 25, and `"hot"` at 25 or above.

title: Create entry
instruction: Implement `create_entry(timestamp: String, message: String) -> String`. Consume both strings and return `"[timestamp] message"`, with one space after `]`. Empty inputs produce `"[] "`.

title: Prefix entry
instruction: Implement `prefix_entry(prefix: String, entry: String) -> String`. Consume both strings and return `"prefix: entry"`, with one space after the colon.

title: Analyze
instruction: Implement `analyze(text: &str) -> (usize, usize, usize, bool)`. Return, in order: whitespace-separated word count; Unicode character count including spaces; count of individual `.`, `!`, and `?` characters; whether any `?` occurs. Empty input returns `(0, 0, 0, false)`.

title: Remove duplicates
instruction: Implement `remove_duplicates(v: &mut Vec<i32>)`. Keep only the first occurrence of each value, preserving original order. `[3, 1, 3, 2, 1] → [3, 1, 2]`; empty input stays empty.

title: Normalize
instruction: Implement `normalize(v: &mut Vec<f64>)`. For nonnegative, finite inputs, divide each value by the largest value. `[1, 2, 3] → [1/3, 2/3, 1]`. Leave empty and all-zero vectors unchanged.

title: Truncate words
instruction: Implement `truncate_words(s, max_words)`. Return at most the first `max_words` whitespace-separated words, joined with single spaces. A limit of 0 or empty input returns `""`.

title: Contains word
instruction: Implement `contains_word(text, word)`. Return true if a whitespace-separated token exactly equals `word`. Matching is case-sensitive and punctuation remains part of the token. Empty `word` returns false.

chapter_label: Chapter 5 — Using Structs to Structure Related Data
title: New
instruction: Implement `BankAccount::new(owner, initial_balance)`. Store an owned copy of the name and the initial balance. Assume a nonnegative finite initial balance.

chapter_label: Chapter 5 — Using Structs to Structure Related Data
title: Deposit
instruction: Implement `deposit(&mut self, amount)`. Add positive finite amounts to the balance. Ignore zero and negative amounts.

chapter_label: Chapter 5 — Using Structs to Structure Related Data
title: Withdraw
instruction: Implement `withdraw(&mut self, amount) -> bool`. For positive finite amounts no larger than the balance, subtract the amount and return true. Otherwise return false without changing the balance.

chapter_label: Chapter 5 — Using Structs to Structure Related Data
title: Balance
instruction: Implement `balance(&self) -> f64`. Return the current balance without consuming the account.

chapter_label: Chapter 5 — Using Structs to Structure Related Data
title: Statement
instruction: Implement `statement(&self) -> String`. Return `"owner: $balance"`, formatting the balance with exactly two decimal places. Example: `"Alice: $70.00"`.

title: Area
instruction: Implement `area(&shape)`. Circle: πr². Rectangle: width × height. Triangle: Heron’s formula, where `s = (a+b+c)/2` and area = √(s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)). Call area only for valid shapes.

title: Describe
instruction: Implement `describe(&shape)`. Return `"Circle with radius R"`, `"Rectangle W x H"`, or `"Triangle with sides A, B, C"`. Use ordinary number formatting.

title: Is valid
instruction: Implement `is_valid(&shape)`. Require positive finite dimensions. For triangles, also require each pair of sides to sum to more than the third side. Equality is invalid.

title: Parse age
instruction: Implement `parse_age(s) -> Option<u32>`. Accept integer text from 0 through 150 inclusive. Return None for empty input, invalid unsigned integer text, surrounding whitespace, or a value above 150.

title: Greet
instruction: Implement `greet(name: Option<&str>) -> String`. Some(name) returns `"Hello, name!"`; None returns `"Hello, stranger!"`. Some("") returns `"Hello, !"`.

title: Find matching
instruction: Implement `find_matching(v, prefix)`. Return a shared reference to the first string starting with the case-sensitive prefix, or None. An empty prefix matches the first string; an empty slice returns None. Keep the provided lifetime signature.

title: Validate name
instruction: Implement `validate_name(name)`. Empty input returns NameEmpty; more than 50 Unicode characters returns NameTooLong. Otherwise return the original borrowed name. Do not trim input.

title: Validate age
instruction: Implement `validate_age(age_str)`. Parse as u32 without trimming. Parse failures return AgeNotANumber. Values below 18 return AgeTooYoung; above 120 return AgeTooOld. Accept 18 through 120 inclusive.

title: Create profile
instruction: Implement `create_profile(name, age_str)`. Validate the name first, then the age, using `?`. Return `"Name: name, Age: age"` on success. If both inputs are invalid, return the name error first.

chapter_label: Chapter 8.1 — Storing Lists of Values with Vectors
title: Longer than five
instruction: Implement `longer_than_five(words)`. Count words with more than 5 Unicode characters. Empty input returns 0.

chapter_label: Chapter 8.1 — Storing Lists of Values with Vectors
title: Starts ab
instruction: Implement `starts_ab(words)`. Return owned copies of words beginning with lowercase a or b, preserving order. Empty strings do not match.

chapter_label: Chapter 8.1 — Storing Lists of Values with Vectors
title: Longest
instruction: Implement `longest(words)`. Borrow the longest word by Unicode character count. On ties return the first. Empty input returns `""`. Keep the lifetime signature.

chapter_label: Chapter 8.1 — Storing Lists of Values with Vectors
title: Joined
instruction: Implement `joined(words)`. Join all entries with `", "`, preserving empty entries. Empty input returns `""`.

chapter_label: Chapter 8.1 — Storing Lists of Values with Vectors
title: First letters
instruction: Implement `first_letters(words)`. Return the first Unicode character of each nonempty word, preserving order. Skip empty strings.

chapter_label: Chapter 8.1 — Storing Lists of Values with Vectors
title: Contains e
instruction: Implement `contains_e(words)`. Count words containing lowercase e at least once; repeated e characters count only once per word.

title: Make adder
instruction: Implement `make_adder(n)`. Return a closure that adds captured n to its argument. It must still work after the function returns.

title: Make multiplier
instruction: Implement `make_multiplier(n)`. Return a closure that multiplies its argument by captured n.

title: Pipeline
instruction: Implement `pipeline(v, ops)`. For each value, apply the operations in slice order and collect the results. No operations returns a copy of v; empty input stays empty.

chapter_label: Chapter 10 — Generic Types, Traits, and Lifetimes
title: Channels
instruction: Implement `channel_name` for both types. EmailNotifier returns `"email"`; SlackNotifier returns `"slack"`.

chapter_label: Chapter 10 — Generic Types, Traits, and Lifetimes
title: Send
instruction: Implement `send` for both types as console output only. Email: `"Email to ADDRESS: MESSAGE"`. Slack: `"Slack #CHANNEL: MESSAGE"`. No real messages are sent.

chapter_label: Chapter 10 — Generic Types, Traits, and Lifetimes
title: Broadcast
instruction: Implement `broadcast(notifiers, message)`. Call send once on each notifier in order. The generic slice holds one concrete notifier type. Empty input prints nothing.

chapter_label: Chapter 10 — Generic Types, Traits, and Lifetimes
title: Notify all
instruction: Implement `notify_all(notifiers, message)`. Call send once per trait object in order. This slice can contain different notifier types. Empty input prints nothing.

title: Sorted copy
instruction: Implement private `stats::sorted_copy(v)`. Return a sorted copy in ascending order, preserving the input. Assume finite values. Empty input returns an empty vector.

title: Mean
instruction: Implement public `stats::mean(v)`. Return Some(sum / count) for a nonempty slice, otherwise None. Assume finite values.

title: Median
instruction: Implement public `stats::median(v)`. Sort a copy. For an odd count return the middle value; for an even count return the average of the two middle values. Empty input returns None.

title: Mode
instruction: Implement public `stats::mode(v)`. Return the most frequent value. Break ties by choosing the smallest value. Empty input returns None.
